# [PROJECT_NAME]-AI — AI knowledge base and workspace of [PROJECT_NAME]

<!-- Generated by /start from .ai/templates/KB-README.template.md. Remove the [BRACKETS]. -->

The knowledge base that AI agents use when working on **[PROJECT_NAME]** ([one-line purpose, from
the services' READMEs or catalog]): the system and each of its services, the contracts between
them, one file per Jira ticket, the known issues — plus the working methodology itself and the
opencode wiring to install.

**It is cloned as `.ai/` inside the workspace** — a plain folder (not a git repository) that also
holds the code of each service, cloned beside `.ai/`. You launch opencode in that folder. Nothing
from this repository is ever committed to a service.

## Services of this workspace

| Service | Repository | Clone as |
|---|---|---|
| [service-a] | `[url]` | `[service-a]/` |
| [service-b] | `[url]` | `[service-b]/` |

## Set up your workspace

Once per developer, in the folder that holds (or will hold) the services — e.g. `[PROJECT_NAME]/`:

```powershell
git clone <url of this repository> .ai
powershell -File .ai\install\install-opencode.ps1
Copy-Item .ai\hooks\pre-commit-guard.sh .ai\.git\hooks\pre-commit
git clone [url of service-a] [service-a]
git clone [url of service-b] [service-b]
```

Linux, WSL or macOS:

```bash
git clone <url of this repository> .ai
bash .ai/install/install-opencode.sh
cp .ai/hooks/pre-commit-guard.sh .ai/.git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .ai/.git/hooks/pre-commit
git clone [url of service-a] [service-a]
git clone [url of service-b] [service-b]
```

Skip the service clones you already have there. The installer runs once per machine (it serves
every workspace) — run it again after a `git -C .ai pull` that changed `.ai/install/`. With the
ai-core repository at hand, `install.ps1 -Remote <url of this repository>` (bash:
`install.sh --remote <url of this repository>`) does the first three lines.

Then open opencode **in that folder** — never inside a service folder — and run the command of your
ticket: `/analysis <key>`, `/bugfix <key>` or `/adaptive <key>`. Day-to-day reference:
`.ai/HOW_TO.md`.

## What is in here

Paths as the workspace sees them (GitLab shows them without the `.ai/` prefix).

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `.ai/non-negotiables.md` · `.ai/install/` | The rules in force with or without a command · the installer of the opencode wiring (instructions, 10 commands, 5 agents, optional permission baseline) |
| `.ai/orchestrator.md` | The system: services table (folder, type, base branch, gate, owner), common conventions, routing |
| `.ai/integrations.md` | Who provides and who consumes each contract; shared resources; dependencies outside the workspace |
| `.ai/CONTEXT.md` | Project-level context that changes rarely — permanent decisions, manual (integration) test procedures, technical data. Changed by its own pull request |
| `.ai/services/<name>/` | `service.md` — the facts of one service — and its `context/` (architecture, data model, API) |
| `.ai/tickets/` | One file per Jira ticket (`<Jira key>.md`): services touched, state, decisions, dead ends, analysis, verification, session log |
| `.ai/known-issues/` | One file per confirmed issue (`<Jira key>.md`), for every service — searched before every analysis |
| `.ai/skills/` | Business workflows, across services |
| `.ai/plans/` | `/architect` plans (`<Jira key>-plan.md`) |
| `.ai/MEMORY.local.md` | Each developer's personal journal and time — **git-ignored (`.gitignore`), never committed**; it exists only on your machine |
| `.ai/METHODOLOGY.md` `HOW_TO.md` `routing.md` `session/` `commands/` `procedures/` `rules/` `policies/` `templates/` `examples/` `hooks/` `install/` `non-negotiables.md` · `.gitignore` `.gitattributes` `.gitlab/` | The methodology itself — generic, identical in every `*-AI` repository |
| `<service>/` | **Not part of this repository**: each service's own git repository, cloned beside `.ai/` |

Paths written inside these files are relative to the workspace folder (the agent's working
directory): `.ai/…` for knowledge, `<service>/…` for code.

## Committing

Changes to the knowledge base are committed **here** — `git -C .ai …` from the workspace folder —
by a person; the agent never commits, neither here nor in a service.

- **Ticket work** happens on a branch `feature/<Jira key>` of this repository — the same name as the
  code branches in the services the ticket touches — created from `master`:
  `git -C .ai switch -c feature/<Jira key> master`. You commit the ticket file (and its plan, its
  known issue, the context and integrations files the ticket changed) when you want — the command
  proposes the message with `git -C .ai add <paths>`, by path. The pull request to `master` (template in `.gitlab/`) is opened at
  `waiting-validation` (analysis delivered, waiting for EUIPO validation — the ticket stays open) and
  at close. After a merge, work on the same ticket resumes on a new `feature/<Jira key>` branch
  created from `master`. The agent never commits and never checks what you committed.
- **Commit messages** start with the Jira key, like the code commits, with no mention of AI and no
  trailers — e.g. `EUIPOBO-21324: closed — code-defect, known issue added`.
- **`CONTEXT.md`, `orchestrator.md`, `integrations.md`, `services/`, `skills/`** change in their own
  pull request, not mixed with a ticket's. The methodology files and the wiring change only by a
  methodology update.
- **`MEMORY.local.md`** is never committed (`.gitignore`).
